# OverDrive CEO Steve Potash Transitions to New Role

OverDrive announced leadership transition with founder and CEO Steve Potash named Chairman of the Board. Marc DeBevoise will become next OverDrive CEO. [...] As OverDrive marks its 40th year in business, founder Steve Potash is embarking on a significant leadership transition, moving from his long-held role as CEO to become the Chairman of the Board. Marc DeBevoise, a veteran media and technology executive who was named President of OverDrive in March, will be his successor. This shift, announced on June 23, signals a new chapter for the company and a personal evolution for Potash, as he moves away from day-to-day operations to focus on global advocacy for literacy, support for public learning institutions, and promoting universal access to knowledge. [...] ## Ensuring a Strong Legacy and Future

In preparing for his transition, Potash emphasized the need for company leadership to truly understand the transformative power of libraries. "OverDrive is never the star—the hero is the librarian," says Potash. "Every major milestone or advance in our service has been because of a brilliant librarian who challenged us to either solve a pain point or to experiment."

Potash's new role will allow him to leverage more than 40 years of experience as an entrepreneur to champion the essential role of libraries in workforce development and informed communities. He says he wants to advance data-driven advocacy to demonstrate the ROI of library services and ensure libraries are recognized for their critical role in community and workforce stability.

OverDrive Names Marc DeBevoise President, Expanding Support for Libraries and Schools  ## OverDrive Names Marc DeBevoise President, Expanding Support for Libraries and Schools

by  mstoneburner@overdrive.com   March 3, 2026

2026, Press Releases

Bringing decades of digital leadership to strengthen OverDrive’s mission for libraries and schools. 

CLEVELAND, OH — March 3, 2026 — As OverDrive — home to Libby, Sora, and Kanopy — moves into its next chapter, the company today announced that Marc DeBevoise has been named President and appointed to the Board of Directors. [...] “Every day, librarians and educators turn effort into impact. Marc shares that spirit, and his leadership will help us make Libby, Sora, and Kanopy even more user friendly, more inclusive, and more joyful to use,” said Steve Potash, Founder & CEO of OverDrive. “He’s spent his career helping people connect with the stories and ideas that move them, and he’s joining us to help libraries and schools do what they do best, change lives through reading, viewing, and learning.” [...] As libraries and schools navigate rising demand for digital access, scarce budgets, increasing expectations for accessibility, and the need for high-quality content across books, audiobooks, and video, DeBevoise will guide OverDrive’s continued investment in tools, partnerships, and product innovation that support educators, librarians, and learners.

# OverDrive Names Marc Debevoise President

An OverDrive rep said Debevoise will focus on “operational leadership and execution," while founder and CEO Steve Potash will "continue to set the long-term vision and overall strategic direction for the company."

Andrew Richard Albanese

#### Andrew Richard Albanese

OverDrive Names Marc Debevoise President

OverDrive this week announced a key appointment, naming former CBS and BrightCove executive Marc DeBevoise as President.

In this new role, DeBevoise will guide OverDrive's “continued investment in tools, partnerships, and product innovation that support educators, librarians, and learners,” according to a company release. He will also join the company’s Board of Directors. [...] "Libraries and schools are where curiosity becomes understanding," DeBevoise said, in a statement. "I am excited to support this community and to help OverDrive expand access to the full spectrum of stories and ideas available through the books, audiobooks, films, and documentaries that entertain and enlighten every reader and deepen learning for every student."
